comments.author: TheReviewerWildTake
comments.body:
In the original video, she (a woman who is talking in the second part of the vid) asked 3 devs on fiverr to do same demo, but with different budgets (one costed 5$, second was 200$ and then 700$) .  
  
So in a way, it wouldn\`t be what actual game developer would do when he needs someone\`s help on a specific part of the game.

If you are a dev, then you aren\`t buying random demos ofc, you are trying to buy time and expertise from people, who can deliver results faster, in a very specific task.  
  
Whether they work with AI or not - is somewhat secondary. The main question here, is whether they know what they are doing, and thus whether they save you money and time.  
If someone has mastered animation with AI and can produce predictable, easy to modify, clean results - great. Their paycheck might be totally worth it, instead of kicking your own model and trying to force it to do something that is completely unfamiliar to you.  


Now, whether you can actually JUDGE  freelancer\`s work properly is a completely different question.   
Ironically, this is why you need to go beyond vibe-coding yourself, if you are serious about gamedev, so that when you depend on someone\`s else work - you at least can see whether they had expertise to do it properly or not.  
If all you know is to prompt - you won\`t know when you see slop, you won\`t know whether person has used lots of assets or had made a custom things etc etc.

You are just exploring some absurd scenarios , click-bait videos or just dealing with people who are fooling around with tools and burning hobby money because it is not big deal for them.

comments.author: Horror-Detective4138
comments.body: Part of the reason you would use AI over paying someone to do it, is the ability to customize everything exactly the way you want it. Not only that, but the history of everything and how it was created will exist in an .md document. You develop workflows and learn how to work better with the AI. I'm not saying you shouldn't use a developer to help with things that AI might struggle with, but overall I'd go the AI option first.
